_provenance.method: the arbiter's own invariants() SQL and api._public, driven against the live estate database on one pinned connection whose synthetic leases were rolled back
_provenance.scope: `live` and `backlog` only. Both predate ADR-0077 and therefore carry neither `waiting_reason` nor `oldest_unexplained_wait_seconds`. They are KEPT AS THAT SHAPE rather than re-captured: a payload from a producer that does not publish the discriminator is the fallback path's only real specimen, and inventing one by deleting keys from a new capture would test this repository's idea of an old producer instead of an old producer.

_provenance_adr_0077.method: `live_2026_08_30` is GET http://127.0.0.1:8400/api/queue/invariants off the wire, no write of any kind. The three states are Arbiter.submit -> Arbiter.tick -> Arbiter.invariants run in estate-manager's own venv against a scratch database this capture created and dropped -- never the live `estate` one, which estate rule 1 forbids writing and which two connections could not have been rolled back across anyway. Only public symbols were touched; the systemd and sampler stand-ins were written against the interface Arbiter calls.
_provenance_adr_0077.synthetic: The waiter's `requested_at` is pushed 1038 s into the past -- the top of the 915-1038 s band estate-manager measured over five nights -- and `holder_overdue`'s `hold_deadline` one minute into the past. Both are the producer's own test idiom for the same reason: waiting out a real clock would make this a slow test of a clock. Everything derived from those rows is theirs. The totals are consequently synthetic here; `live_2026_08_30` is where the live ones are.
